findings.category: continuity / staging regression introduced by the r1 repair
findings.gate: Craft Core reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); Charter §2.8 Injury Persists / unified gate 13; packet obligations.must_include #3

draft_evidence.quote: Then he picked up the first box, and put it on the good shoulder, and went back across the yard toward the inn's door and the morning and the stair and the hole under the city where a woman was reading a wall

comparison_evidence.quote: Brom picked up the box while the factor was still talking. He put it on the shoulder that was not the good one, because the good one had just paid for a cart and he knew it, and he would carry the bound one wrong for a day and say nothing, and Cael entered the debt where debts went.

findings.consequence: Brom picks up the same box twice, five lines apart, and puts it on a different shoulder each time. L57 gives him exactly one box in the yard ('a box set down carefully at his feet'), and Ch10 L101 fixes the carrying order that makes Brom's the first box and Cael's the middle one, so 'the box' at L75 and 'the first box' at L79 are the same object; there is no second box on the page for him to lift. The reader therefore watches an action that cannot be staged. Worse, the second lift cancels the first one's meaning: L75 is the F-005 repair — the good shoulder has just paid for the cart, so the load goes on the bound one and Cael enters the debt — and L79 puts the load straight back on the good shoulder, erasing the cost the pass was written to ledger. STATE_RUNNING's Ch12 row inherits from here ('Brom's rock and back (the good shoulder used wrong; the bound one carried)'), so the contradiction does not stay local: Ch12 opens from a state this chapter now asserts twice, incompatibly. It sits in the chapter's most load-bearing repaired beat.
findings.repair_target: Delete the second pickup. L79 should carry Brom away from the yard on the load he already has — 'Then he went back across the yard toward the inn's door and the morning and the stair and the hole under the city where a woman was reading a wall' — leaving L75 as the single lift and the single shoulder. Do not resolve it the other way by cutting L75: that clause is the F-005 ledger and the hook Ch12 pays. If a second box is genuinely wanted, it must be established at L57 before the factor speaks.

The author report's deviations state 'STATE_RUNNING corrected', so the discrepancy is currently invisible to the next seat. The concrete cost is downstream: Ch12's packet is built from this row and opens on the 290th, and any Ch12 or Ch13 seat reading the row will believe the chamber week was dramatized through the 289th and will date Cleon's 'Give me a week' from the wrong end.

findings.category: physical continuity inside the new staging
findings.gate: Craft Core reader-trust invariant 2 (causal legibility); Charter §4.1 (physical space reconstructable)

draft_evidence.quote: It had come through the yard's gate too fast, by the evidence — a wheel in the drain, the bed over, the load on the stones — and the carter was at the beast's head with the traces fouled

comparison_evidence.quote: and the bed came up, and hung, and the good shoulder said something Cael saw in the set of it and Brom did not, and the cart went back onto its wheels with the load on and stood there

findings.consequence: Cael's read of the wreck at L59 lists the load as down on the paving — it is one of the three pieces of 'evidence' he catalogues, alongside the wheel and the tipped bed, and 'the load on the stones' reads as spilled. Four lines later the cart is righted 'with the load on', which requires the load to have stayed aboard. The r1 text carried only the second reading ('gone over on its side with the load on'), so the ambiguity is new to this pass. It matters more than its size because the weight of what Brom lifted is precisely the quantity the scene now turns on: F-005's repair prices the feat, and a reader who takes L59 literally sees an empty bed being lifted and a bill charged for it, while a reader who takes L63 literally has to un-see a spilled load nobody reloaded.
findings.repair_target: Make the two lines agree. Simplest is to change L59's third item so the load is still aboard and bearing on the ground — 'a wheel in the drain, the bed over, the load hard against the stones' — which keeps Cael's three-item catalogue and the weight both. Alternatively, if the load did spill, L63 must lose 'with the load on' and the scene must account for who put it back.

strengths: The repair did the hard thing rather than the cheap thing. F-001 asked for the yard staged and F-009 asked for the word count recovered by staging rather than padding, and the pass delivered exactly that: ~800 words of pluperfect report at L57–L73 in r1 are replaced by a scene, and the chapter moved from 3,907 words to 4,074 without a single line of filler. Every one of the 167 recovered words is dramatized action or spoken dialogue.

The factor's offer (L71) is the best new writing in the pass and does world-discipline work the report version could not: 'I've a yard here and a second on the second tier, and I've no one in either who could have done that without a Path, and two who couldn't have done it with one.' It prices Brom by what the city cannot buy, then converts a Copper's paper into a wage, a named pass and a bed inside the second wall — charter §6.5, the Path system visibly deforming an economy — and closes on 'You'd be ranked, here. You'd be what you are,' which is the temptation stated as a kindness. The man is never a straw offer.

The decline is staged as an action inside another man's sentence — 'Brom picked up the box while the factor was still talking' (L75) — which is the card's 'the book lets the choice be the whole statement' executed at the level of timing rather than paraphrase. L81's couplet then survives in its proper role, as Cael's log line after the fact instead of the substitute for the fact.

F-005's repair is the model of how to bill a feat without narrating pain: 'the foot with the tooth-hole in it taking the brace on the stones, and the bed came up, and hung, and the good shoulder said something Cael saw in the set of it and Brom did not' (L63). The cost is carried by a verb ('hung') and by a thing the character does not himself notice, and it is entered forward as a debt at L75 rather than dissolved. If E2-001 is fixed, this passage becomes the chapter's second-best paragraph.

The Seln recast (L109) is a better sentence than the one it replaces and repairs two findings with one move. 'the grit on a boot, which Cael had heard on the floor and not seen, said a roof' gives the supposition a physical foot to stand on; 'not to the crown; Seln did not stand beside a thing that read bodies' actively corrects the r1 geometry instead of quietly deleting it; and the station's light now sits above him, which restores the tiered city's argument about who stands where and keeps the Arbiter station at the distance the party's whole Treswick discipline depends on.

The two smallest repairs are the most disciplined. 'so far as he could tell' (L9) closes F-010 by converting a verdict into Cael's fallibility in five words and nothing else moves; 'against a post across the river' (L25) closes F-006 by identifying the post instead of measuring it, which is what the payoff needed all along. F-008's fix relocates a beat rather than deleting it, so the fixed line is unbroken and the beat is kept.

The whole demonstration sequence and the whole close came through the pass untouched — L13–L45, L49–L51, L113, L117–L129 and L135 are byte-identical to r1. A continuity-repair run that changes only what the findings named is the discipline Craft Core's revision section asks for, and this one held it.
